description:
We are HTTP POLARIS, a team of Colombian students passionate about software development, innovation, and technology with purpose. We believe that great ideas can become powerful solutions when curiosity meets collaboration.

Inspired by the star that guides explorers, we aim to transform data into knowledge, technology into opportunities, and innovation into positive impact.

We don't just observe a changing world. We build tools to understand it.
summary: Earth Waltz is an open-source web application that translates NASA-ISRO NISAR radar data into plain language, so anyone can understand how Earth's surface is changing without being a remote sensing expert. A Python pipeline processes NISAR synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery to compute backscatter, change detection, and area statistics, and a large language model (LLM) turns those verified results into clear explanations adapted to each audience. Our first module, "First Dance: Mangroves," studies the mangroves of the Ciénaga Grande de Santa Marta in Colombia, a Ramsar wetland affected by hydrological and salinity changes. Users can learn how to read a radar image, get an automated report of what the scene shows, and compare it with another date. The modular design allows new "dances" (floods, wildfires, glaciers, land subsidence) to be added, making NISAR data accessible to educators, managers, and communities.
details:
Earth Waltz: Turning radar data into stories about our changing planet.

What it does and how it works
Earth Waltz is an interactive web application that turns complex NISAR radar data into clear, plain-language stories about how the land surface changes. Our first module, “First Dance: Mangroves,” focuses on the Ciénaga Grande de Santa Marta in Colombia, the largest coastal lagoon complex in the country and a mangrove ecosystem under real environmental pressure.

A Python pipeline reads 16 NISAR GSLC scenes, crops a 53,000-hectare study area, processes the HH and HV polarizations, and averages 4×4 pixel blocks to reduce speckle noise. It converts power to decibels, classifies open water with an HV threshold of −20.78 dB, and filters out change patches smaller than roughly 1 hectare. The pipeline then compares scenes. It uses 12-day pairs with the same processing version as the reference, and it also compares the first and last scenes of each processing version. It produces color radar images, change maps (red for areas that became water, blue for areas that stopped being water), and hectare-level statistics. A Node.js/Express server exposes these results through an API and sends the summarized data to a large language model (Gemini). The model writes an explanation in everyday language, including key findings, what the results mean, what we do not know, and a glossary. If the AI call fails, the app falls back to the report computed by the pipeline, so users always get a result. Users can explore the radar images, compare different dates, and read the report without any remote-sensing background.

Benefits and intended impact
Radar data is powerful, but it is hard for non-experts to read. Earth Waltz makes it accessible to students, communities, journalists, and local decision-makers by showing how radar images work, what changed between dates, and how reliable that information is. The tool is designed to support environmental awareness and conversations about wetland and mangrove monitoring in a region where these ecosystems matter for biodiversity, fisheries, and local livelihoods. The app is also built to grow. “First Dance: Mangroves” is the first of five planned “dances,” each covering a different Earth phenomenon.

Scientific honesty
We deliberately state what the analysis can and cannot do. It measures open water from the radar signal. It does not, by itself, determine mangrove loss or gain, detect water beneath tree canopies, or identify the causes of change. Comparisons across different processing versions are flagged as not directly comparable. These warnings are shown to users as part of the interpretation.

Tools and technologies

  • Data: NASA-ISRO NISAR GSLC scenes (L-band SAR, HH and HV polarizations)
  • Analysis: Python (h5py, NumPy, SciPy, pyproj, Matplotlib)
  • Back end: Node.js and Express, with a cached API layer
  • AI: Google Gemini (LLM) for plain-language explanations, with a template-based fallback
  • Front end: HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with animations and a custom visual identity
  • Visuals: AI-generated illustrations for banners, and original photographs of the Ciénaga Grande taken by team members

Creativity
Earth Waltz frames the dialogue between the Earth and the satellite as a dance. Each phenomenon is a “dance,” and the radar is the partner that lets us follow its steps. This storytelling approach, combined with an AI narrator that explains data honestly and simply, turns a technical product into an experience people want to explore.

Factors our team considered

  • Accessibility: language and design that anyone can understand
  • Scientific rigor: clear limitations and warnings instead of overstated claims
  • Reliability: a fallback report if the AI service is unavailable
  • Security: the API key stays on the server and is never exposed in the browser
  • Scalability: a modular design so new dances and regions can be added
  • Ethics and attribution: clear labeling of AI-generated illustrations versus original photographs

Team HTTP Polaris
Andrea Valentina Granados García (front end, user experience design, banners, animations) and Jesús Múnera (back end, Python radar pipeline, AI explanation server).
dataRefs: NASA Earthdata Search: data discovery, search, visualization, and access across NASA’s Earth science data
ASF Data Search (Vertex): NASA’s archive of SAR data, including NISAR scenes
NISAR Data User Guide: how to find, access, and work with NISAR data
Intro to Remote Sensing (NASA Earthdata): basics of remotely sensed data, resolution types, and processing
Intro to Synthetic Aperture Radar (NASA Earthdata): SAR basics, frequency, wavelength, polarization, and scattering mechanisms
NISAR StoryMaps: interactive stories on SAR applications for floods, wildfires, land subsidence, oil slicks, and glacial motion
NISAR Applications White Papers: two-page overviews of NISAR applications with societal benefit
UAVSAR Postcards: false-color composites of airborne UAVSAR data showing Earth processes
